methodological_rigor.justification: This in vitro study uses two CRC cell lines (HCT116, HT29) with orthogonal approaches (pharmacologic FH535 + siRNA β-catenin knockdown) to test pathway specificity and downstream chemokine effects, which is a methodological strength. Assays (MTT, CV, Annexin/PI flow cytometry, cell cycle, wound healing with mitomycin C pretreatment, Matrigel invasion, Western, RT-qPCR, ELISA, THP-1 polarization, TCGA in silico) are standard and appropriate. Limitations include no in vivo validation, FH535 is known to also target PPARs (acknowledged), only two cell lines without primary cells or organoids, no dose-response over time for all endpoints, and no CRISPR or selective Wnt inhibitor confirmation. Three biological replicates per assay.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Pre-clinical in vitro mechanistic study with TCGA in silico analysis; any translational path to CRC therapy is speculative, and FH535 is a tool compound rather than a drug candidate. The connection between Wnt/β-catenin inhibition and MCP1/MCP2 suppression is biologically interesting but the implications for immune therapy in CRC require in vivo and patient validation. Oxford LoE 5 for preclinical in vitro work.

reporting_quality.justification: ARRIVE is the closest applicable standard for preclinical work, though ARRIVE primarily targets animal studies and this is purely in vitro (no mouse/rat work). Methods are detailed for most assays (antibody catalog numbers, software versions, replicate counts). Weaknesses include no blinding of analysts, no formal randomization for well allocation, no statement on replicate handling for Western blot quantification beyond 'densitometry', no explicit power calculation, and no data/code availability statement. Supplementary figures referenced for MCP1/MCP2 and THP-1 polarization data.

novelty_literature.justification: FH535 has been extensively characterized in CRC, HCC, pancreatic, breast, and osteosarcoma contexts (cited Refs 15-19, 23-25), and Wnt/β-catenin-mediated chemokine regulation has been explored in other systems. The specific novelty is the demonstration that β-catenin regulates MCP1/CCL2 and MCP2/CCL8 in CRC (claimed by authors as 'first time'), corroborated by siRNA knockdown and THP-1 M1 polarization evidence. The in silico TCGA analysis adds modest translational framing. The contribution is a meaningful incremental mechanistic extension.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is organized and scientifically clear with detailed figure legends and methods. Some language is overly verbose in the Discussion with repeated framing of 'precision oncology' and 'chemokine-mediated tumor-immune crosstalk'. Minor issues include an incorrect 'MCP8' reference that appears to be a typo for MCP2 (Results section on in silico analysis), and some redundant sentences in the Discussion. Figures are well described with statistical thresholds reported.

key_strengths: Two CRC cell lines (HCT116, HT29) tested with concordant pharmacologic (FH535) and genetic (siRNA) approaches
Multiple endpoints assessed: viability, migration, invasion, apoptosis, cell cycle, Western, RT-qPCR, ELISA
Novel link between Wnt/β-catenin inhibition and MCP1/MCP2 chemokine suppression with THP-1 M1-like polarization evidence
TCGA/UALCAN/TIMER2.0 in silico analysis extends findings to patient data
Mitomycin C pretreatment for wound healing to control for proliferation
key_concerns: Only two cell lines tested; no primary CRC cells, organoids, or in vivo validation
FH535 is a non-selective inhibitor (also targets PPARs); authors acknowledge but do not add CRISPR or selective Wnt inhibitor confirmation
Apparent typo 'MCP8' for MCP2 in Results section
No data/code availability statement; no ARRIVE checklist explicitly cited
Functional impact on TME assessed only indirectly via THP-1 conditioned-media polarization
Discussion is repetitive and could be tightened
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid mechanistic in vitro study with both pharmacologic and genetic validation and a modestly novel β-catenin-chemokine link; fits a Tier 3 molecular oncology journal after minor revisions addressing the MCP8 typo and ideally adding selective inhibitor or CRISPR validation.
